doc.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Charleston's lost jazz centre and the Jenkins Orphanage
summary: He says New Orleans took over from Charleston, and points to the Jenkins Orphanage which produced many trumpeters.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well Charleston, South Carolina should have been the jazz center of the world. No, they decided to push slavery, cotton and rice. It’s like I said today, I’ll bet you a million dollars you can’t find 20 black musicians who would have brought this subject up today. I don’t care where they graduated from or how good they look or where they’re going. They don’t want to bring it up. They don’t want to offend anybody. That’s not your concern. If I offend you that’s your problem. I’m telling the story. I hope I offend you, maybe you’ll pay attention. So I’m saying so New Orleans took over because the merchants promoted jazz. They promoted it, the Creoles promoted. Charleston had to go. And I was born in Charleston, and that’s my only regret. I wish I was born there. So I

spent way too long wading in the water. You know? It comes from the cotton plantation and slavery. Somehow the music culture of Charleston survived. Thank God. Because of Jenkins Orphanage. You heard about that orphanage? Daniel Jenkins Orphanage. Look up and study on Daniel Jenkins Orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina. Jabbo Smith came out of there, Cat Anderson, most of the great trumpet players, you know, have passed through the orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina.
And you’re going back there very soon.
